newsitem.title: USA: U.S. bulk millfeeds - Prices firm, demand eases.
newsitem.headline: U.S. bulk millfeeds - Prices firm, demand eases.

text.p: U.S. millfeed prices remained firm in most markets after posting strong gains Wednesday, however demand had eased since then, millfeed dealers said.
Supplies remained tight for prompt shipment, which has prevented some dealers from completing sales.
"There are still people who would buy stuff if I could find it," said a north Texas dealer.
Buffalo values rose in reaction to some flour mills scheduled to be shut down soon for fumigation.
CBOT corn and soymeal futures were lower Thursday, which may have tempered demand.
Many dealers said sharply higher CBOT corn and soymeal futures Wednesday sparked small-scale panic buying of millfeeds amid ideas feed prices would move higher.

Kansas City rail offers rose $1.00 to $56.00. Dealers said buying had eased from Wednesday's strong level. On Wednesday, sources said buying was active because completion of the wheat harvest in southern Kansas and Oklahoma had farmers and ranchers catching up on livestock feed purchases.
